stage_notes:
FULL RE-RANK over the three hypotheses surviving the stage-4 re-run against real MSK-CHORD counts (H-001, H-002, H-009). The prior ranking is void, not amended: it ranked a four-hypothesis set in which H-011 held rank 1, and H-011 has since been rejected as underpowered on real data (minimum detectable per-SD ratio-of-hazard-ratios 1.26 unrestricted / 1.38 panel-restricted against a strongest-form predicted effect of only 1.18-1.25). All nine component scores below were re-derived from the re-run feasibility blocks; no score was carried over. The feasibility component in particular moved DOWN for H-001 (equivalence margin 1.5 TOST / 1.6 on the 95%-CI convention, not the 1.4 the formula-derived run supported; the chemotherapy/STK11-LoF cell is a real 163 and carries 61% of the interaction variance) and for H-002 (gene-versus-gene detectable ratio 1.76, not 1.57, because real STK11/KEAP1 co-occurrence is 50.5% rather than the assumed 30%, shrinking both identifying single-mutant cells).

DID THE RANKING CHANGE? Yes, necessarily at the top: the prior rank 1 no longer exists. H-001 is now rank 1. Among the three survivors the ordering is H-001 (3.375) > H-009 (2.825) > H-002 (2.775). The H-009/H-002 separation is 0.05 and should be read as a near-tie, resolved on feasibility structure rather than on any confidence that one question matters more: H-002's estimand is a difference between two coefficients against a common reference, so Var = 1/E_KEAP1only + 1/E_STK11only and the large double-wildtype cell cancels out entirely - cohort size buys this hypothesis nothing - and its cell sizes additionally rest on a prevalence transfer (KEAP1 prevalence among ICI-treated assumed equal to the NSCLC-wide 13.2%), whereas H-009's four cells are anchored throughout on real co-mutant counts and real per-genotype ICI-exposure rates.

PRIOR-NEGATIVE VERIFICATION. No entry in this file carries a `verified` flag, so the schema's discount rule cannot be applied mechanically. I resolved the ambiguity per entry rather than uniformly, and said so in each scoring_note: an entry citing a named PMID together with a specific effect estimate and confidence interval is treated as verified-equivalent and discounts novelty at full weight (Papillon-Cavanagh PMID 32312757 for H-001, De Giglio PMID 39709652 for H-002, Ricciuti PMID 34740862 for H-009); an entry that is a conference abstract, a preprint, or explicitly flagged as read 'as reported in secondary summaries' is treated as unverified and discounts at roughly half weight (the ASCO 2025 and ASCO 2026 abstracts, the PIONeeR preprint). This resolution is deliberately asymmetric in the direction that penalises: where a citation is precise enough to be checkable, I assumed the ground is covered.

WHAT I WOULD ACTUALLY PRE-REGISTER: H-001, and nothing else in this batch.

H-001 earns a slot for a reason that is not its composite score. It is the only design in the surviving set carrying a non-ICI comparator arm, and the prognostic-versus-predictive question is the axis the entire claim graph turns on; every other survivor is ICI-only and therefore cannot distinguish the two whatever it finds. Its contribution is bounded and, unusually, known in advance: it narrows the published interaction interval from Papillon-Cavanagh's 0.76-1.67 to roughly 0.67-1.50 in a cohort about six times larger and in the chemo-immunotherapy era that postdates that cohort. That is modest, but it is the only one of the three whose value does not depend on the true effect being large, and it is informative either way. Conditions are not optional: the prereg must prespecify the equivalence margin at 1.5 (TOST) or 1.6 (95%-CI convention) - NOT 1.4, and not 1.25 - must prespecify that an interval excluding neither 1.0 nor the margin is INCONCLUSIVE and is reported as such, must fix the interaction scale before unlock, and must report the left-truncation interval distribution by arm before the confirmatory run.

WHAT I WOULD NOT SPEND A SLOT ON, despite ranking it: H-009 and H-002. Both are ranked because the ranking must be contiguous, not because I recommend testing them.

H-009 (rank 2) can resolve only the upper half of the effect range its own literature implies (detects 1.71 at f=0.6 any-line against an implied 1.6-2.0), and only after a population change - any-line with line as a covariate instead of the first-line restriction stage 2 wrote - that alters the question being asked. Its identifying cell is 78 patients any-line, 51 first-line, and it is the cell most depleted by the one MNAR mechanism that runs the wrong way here: KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal across IMPACT panels while STK11 coverage is not. The most probable outcome is an interval that excludes neither the null nor the 1.7 inconclusiveness bound, which under R6 would consume an FDR slot and widen the correction applied to H-001 while returning nothing.

H-002 (rank 3) should not be pre-registered on its stated primary contrast. It detects a gene-versus-gene ratio of 1.76 against published orderings of 1.9-2.0 that come from cohorts of 145 and 343 and are the sort of estimate that regresses; if the true difference is the more likely 1.4-1.5 the design returns an inconclusive result by construction. Its worst measurement problem - differential KEAP1 versus STK11 callability across panel versions - maps one-to-one onto the estimand, which is a between-gene comparison, and the schema publishes no gene-by-panel coverage map to bound it (cost somewhere between 4.2% and 21.3%). The genuinely well-powered part, the KEAP1 main effect at 1.35, is not the hypothesis as written; promoting it to primary would be a different hypothesis that stages 2, 3 and 4 have not evaluated, and doing that here rather than by re-entering the pipeline would be exactly the substitution this stage exists to refuse.

HONEST CONCLUSION ON THE COHORT. This cohort can answer one of the three STK11 questions the pipeline generated, in its equivalence form only, within a margin (0.67-1.50) that some readers will judge too wide to be decisive. It cannot currently adjudicate either the KRAS-conditionality question or the STK11-versus-KEAP1 partition: both are between-cell contrasts resting on identifying cells of 51-86 patients, and both sit at or below the effect size their own literatures imply. That is not a reason to run them anyway with softer conditions; it is the finding. Recommendation: pre-register H-001 alone, which also keeps the batch's FDR denominator at one, and record H-002 and H-009 in the graveyard as adequately motivated but not yet answerable - H-009 becomes viable in a cohort with roughly 2-3x these ICI-treated numbers or crossed with H-001's non-ICI arm, H-002 in one where the single-mutant cells clear ~200 each or where a gene-by-panel coverage manifest bounds the callability asymmetry.

novelty.scoring_note: GAP 2.5. Not a 5. The gap type is 'contradiction' and the contradiction is live - single-arm ICI-only cohorts (C-003, C-039) say predictive, every design with a non-ICI arm (C-012/C-013, C-037/C-038, C-018) says prognostic - but the field is NOT structurally unable to answer it, because Papillon-Cavanagh already had the control arm and already produced this exact estimand. PRIOR-NEGATIVE RESOLUTION (no `verified` flag present): PMID 32312757 cites a named PMID with a specific interaction estimate and interval (OS HR 1.13, 0.76-1.67, p=0.540; PFS 1.05, 0.76-1.44, p=0.785) at n=2276, so I treated it as verified-equivalent and discounted at full weight - somebody looked at precisely this quantity and reported null. PMID 34500370 likewise names a published article whose title states the prognostic interpretation, so the idea is already in print. The ASCO 2025 meta-analysis abstract (n=1596, randomized-comparator null) is a conference abstract with no full paper, so I treated it as unverified and discounted at roughly half weight; it points the same way but I did not let it carry full force. What survives is a precision-and-era gap, not a design gap: the 2020 cohort is non-squamous-only, predates chemo-immunotherapy as the dominant first line, and no verified post-2022 cohort with n>500 reports a formal treatment-by-STK11 interaction. That is real and it is the highest gap score in the surviving set, but it is well short of a 5 and it is only one step above replication. MECHANISM 5.0. Stage 3 verdict 'strong' maps to 4-5; adjusted to the top of the band for specificity, which is the one adjustment the brief names. The causal chain does not merely predict a direction - it predicts that the STK11 hazard is raised in BOTH treatment strata and that their RATIO is null, i.e. it discriminates prognostic from predictive rather than restating the association, and the discriminating contrast is the pre-registered estimand. It is falsified if the STK11 hazard is materially larger in the ICI stratum. This is the case the brief describes as worth more because it makes the test informative either way. FEASIBILITY 2.5, re-derived from the real numbers and NOT carried over. Verdict pass. Real cells 336/2329/163/1844, analysable 185/1281/126/1420 after the stated A1 and A2 multipliers. The equivalence margin is now 1.5 under TOST or 1.6 on the 95%-CI convention, worse than the 1.4 the formula-derived run supported; bounding inside 1.4 would require f>=0.72, inside the 95%-CI reading f>=0.91, neither defensible. Penalties applied: the 163-patient chemotherapy/STK11-LoF cell carries 61% of the interaction variance on its own; two derived multipliers (A1 driver exclusion, A2 first-line share) rest on stated assumptions rather than counts; MNAR co-mutation ascertainment is unresolved because no gene-by-panel coverage map exists, leaving the restriction cost anywhere between 4.2% and 21.3%; ECOG is NLP-extracted with missingness likely differential by arm, on precisely the indication-bias axis stage 3 called the dominant threat; PD-L1 exists only as a binary NLP flag, not a TPS band. No penalty for NLP exposure - the exposure is a variant call, the strongest ascertainment available. Not a 4, because the design detects 1.55 at the reference f and the predictive claim the field asserts implies roughly 1.4, so it cannot detect the effect it is arguing about; that is the edge of detectability. Not a 2, because the equivalence reading it CAN support genuinely narrows the published interval, its cells are the largest among the survivors, and it is the only design here with a non-ICI comparator. ARITHMETIC: 0.4*2.5 + 0.35*5.0 + 0.25*2.5 = 1.000 + 1.750 + 0.625 = 3.375. Rank 1.

GAP 2.0. PRIOR-NEGATIVE RESOLUTION (no `verified` flag present): PMID 34740862 (Ricciuti, JTO 2022, n=1261) is a named PMID with a specific published conclusion - STK11 and KEAP1 confer worse ICI outcomes among KRAS-mutant but not KRAS-wildtype LUAD - so I treated it as verified-equivalent and discounted at full weight. The ASCO 2026 abstract reporting the same KRAS-wildtype null is a conference abstract with no n, so I treated it as unverified and discounted at roughly half weight; it nonetheless points the same way, and two independent sources pointing the same way is what a field looks like when it thinks it already knows the answer. Papillon-Cavanagh (PMID 32312757) does not close this one - it did not stratify by KRAS and is compatible with the interaction being real. So the stratified finding is published at n=1261 and corroborated; what is genuinely absent is the formal product term with a confidence interval, which is the difference between effect modification and two subgroups of unequal size, and which the pipeline's own R5b names as the specific error the STK11 literature makes at scale. That is a real gap but a narrow, methodological one, and adjacent work constrains the answer heavily - the field is not in doubt about the direction, only about the rigour. Below a 3 for that reason; above a 1 because nobody has produced the estimand and the KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell is small in every published cohort, so no prior study could have. MECHANISM 4.0. Stage 3 verdict 'strong' maps to 4-5. Held at the bottom of the band, not raised. The chain is detailed, specific and falsifiable at a named step (KRAS-dependence of the SAM surplus that hyperactivates DNMT1/EZH2 and silences STING), and it predicts a conditional rather than an additive effect, which is a real specificity claim. But the upward adjustment the brief describes is specifically for a mechanism that discriminates ICI-specific from worse-on-any-therapy, and this design cannot deliver it: stage 3 states there is no non-ICI arm and that a real KRAS-by-STK11 interaction may exist on chemotherapy too (C-037 shows a large STK11 effect with no ICI present), and stage 4 repeats that a positive interaction here is prognostic until a non-ICI arm says otherwise. No adjustment up. FEASIBILITY 2.5. Verdict pass, unchanged from the prior run in verdict but re-read from the real counts. Cells anchored on real numbers throughout - kras_and_stk11lof_comutant 385, the KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell a real 331 cohort-wide, and per-genotype ICI-exposure rates computed from by_treatment_exposure (46.9% and 32.8%) rather than assumed - which is the best-anchored derivation among the three and is why this scores above H-002 despite comparable cell sizes. Penalties applied: the any-line specification is REQUIRED to reach 1.71 at f=0.6, and it is a change to the population stage 2 wrote; the first-line specification stage 2 actually asked for detects only 1.94, above most of the implied range; the identifying cell is 78 any-line (51 first-line) and carries 58% of the interaction variance; three derived multipliers (histology, driver exclusion, A2) rest on stated assumptions; MNAR co-mutation runs in the worst direction, since KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal while STK11 coverage is not, so the smallest cell is also the one most depleted by callability and 'STK11-wildtype' on older panels mixes true wildtype with never-tested. No NLP-exposure penalty: exposure and modifier are both variant calls. Set against 1.6-2.0 implied by Ricciuti's stratified pattern, the design resolves the upper half and not the lower half - the edge of detectability, so a 2.5 rather than a 4, and above a 2 only because the real KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell exceeds any published cohort's and the design improves on the state of the art even where it cannot settle the question. ARITHMETIC: 0.4*2.0 + 0.35*4.0 + 0.25*2.5 = 0.800 + 1.400 + 0.625 = 2.825. Rank 2. Ranked second; I would not spend a pre-registration slot on it - see stage_notes.

GAP 3.5 - the highest gap score in the surviving set, and the only component on which this hypothesis leads. PRIOR-NEGATIVE RESOLUTION (no `verified` flag present): PMID 39709652 (De Giglio, Lung Cancer 2025) is a named PMID with a specific multivariable estimate (STK11 HR 1.97, p=0.025, adjusted for KRAS, TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4) so I treated it as verified-equivalent and discounted at full weight - but note what it discounts. It is not a null on this estimand; it is an ANSWER IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION from n=145, standing against the C-CAT cohort's opposite ordering (KEAP1 HR 1.89 with STK11 near null). A prior result that contradicts another prior result does not close a gap, it constitutes one, and that is why this scores above H-001 and H-009 here. The PIONeeR entry is a medRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed, in a second-line-plus population, so I treated it as unverified and discounted at roughly half weight; its double null weakens the premise that either gene carries a large ICI-specific signal but does not settle which carries the shared one. Papillon-Cavanagh's KEAP1-by-treatment null is verified-equivalent and constrains the interpretation to prognostic, which is a real limit on what a win here would mean but not on whether the question is open. Not a 5 because the two conflicting cohorts are small (145 and 343) rather than well-conducted-and-adequately-powered, and because an ICI-only design cannot make whichever gene wins predictive. Close to the structural criterion, though: with 50.5% real co-occurrence, essentially no published cohort is large enough to hold one gene fixed while estimating the other. MECHANISM 2.5. Stage 3 verdict 'moderate' maps to 2-3.5; placed low in the band and not adjusted up. The NRF2 cytoprotection chain is coherent, but it predicts a treatment-INDEPENDENT penalty and the design has no non-ICI arm, so it supplies no specificity of the kind the brief rewards. Worse, stage 3 identifies that part of the predicted pattern is guaranteed by the model form rather than by biology: non-collapsibility of the Cox hazard ratio shifts other coefficients toward the null when any strong prognostic covariate is added, with zero causal contribution from KEAP1, so the hypothesis as literally worded predicts something that would occur anyway. Stage 4 accordingly rules the 'STK11 attenuates relative to unadjusted' limb untestable and forces the single-mutant contrast as primary. A mechanism whose stated prediction is partly an artefact of the estimator is not a 3.5. FEASIBILITY 2.0, re-derived from the real numbers and NOT carried over. Verdict pass, described by stage 4 as 'marginal but defensible, and weaker than the prior run judged'. The detectable gene-versus-gene ratio is 1.76 at f=0.6, not the 1.57 the formula-derived run reported, because real STK11/KEAP1 co-occurrence is 50.5% (512/1013) rather than the assumed 30%, which shrinks both identifying single-mutant cells to 86 and 78. Penalties applied: the estimand is a difference between two coefficients against a common reference, so Var = 1/E_KEAP1only + 1/E_STK11only and the 1009-patient double-wildtype cell cancels out of the variance entirely - the cohort's size buys this hypothesis literally nothing, which makes it the structurally weakest position in the set; the cell derivation rests on a stated prevalence TRANSFER (KEAP1 prevalence among ICI-treated assumed equal to the NSCLC-wide 13.2%) on top of a x0.47 combined restriction, i.e. a derived denominator resting on an assumption rather than a count; MNAR co-mutation ascertainment is acute and maps one-to-one onto the estimand, since a between-gene comparison is corrupted directly by differential KEAP1-versus-STK11 callability and no gene-by-panel coverage map exists to bound it; the KEAP1 x STK11 product term the exposure definition proposes is not powered at all (2.02) and must be excluded from the inferential set. No NLP-exposure penalty: both exposures are variant calls. This is the brief's 'technically feasible but at the edge of detectability' case in its clearest form - 1.76 detectable against published orderings of 1.9-2.0 that come from cohorts of 145 and 343 and would regress to 1.4-1.5, i.e. a design powered to find the effect only at its least plausible magnitude. The well-powered KEAP1 main effect (1.35) is not the hypothesis as written and cannot rescue the score. ARITHMETIC: 0.4*3.5 + 0.35*2.5 + 0.25*2.0 = 1.400 + 0.875 + 0.500 = 2.775. Rank 3. Separated from H-009 by 0.05 - a near-tie broken by feasibility structure, not by any confidence that the question matters less.
